quarters.supplementaryReportName: Q3 2024 Supplementary Regulatory Capital Disclosure (ratios reproduced in Report to Shareholders capital section)

notes.loansToAssetsPct: Computed from loans, net of allowance for loan losses ($971,797M) divided by total assets ($2,076,107M) as disclosed in the same report; not a directly stated ratio.
notes.netIncomeMillions: Net income (attributable to shareholders of the bank; RBC's headline consolidated net income figure).
notes.loanToDepositRatio: Computed: gross loans (Retail $619,452M + Wholesale $358,143M = $977,595M, before allowance) / total deposits ($1,361,265M), both from the Interim Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheet as at July 31, 2024.
notes.wholesaleFundingPct: Computed: RBC's disclosed 'Composition of wholesale funding' table total ($345,178M, which excludes repos) plus balance-sheet 'Obligations related to assets sold under repurchase agreements and securities loaned' ($304,373M) = $649,551M, divided by total assets ($2,076,107M). RBC's own table alone (excl. repo) gives a narrower 16.63%.
notes.retailDepositsPct: From LCR common disclosure template, unweighted 'Retail deposits and deposits from small business customers' ($401,452M) as % of LCR-classified total deposits (retail + operational + non-operational = $819,796M). This LCR classification (quarterly average balances) differs from balance-sheet Personal/Business & government/Bank categorization.
notes.wholesaleDepositsPct: Operational ($170,428M) + Non-operational ($247,916M) deposits / LCR-classified total deposits ($819,796M).
notes.lessStableDepositsPct: LCR 'Less stable deposits' ($271,092M) / LCR-classified total deposits ($819,796M).
notes.operationalDepositsPct: LCR 'Operational deposits (all counterparties)' ($170,428M) / LCR-classified total deposits ($819,796M).
notes.irrbbEveSensitivityPct: RBC discloses only +/-100bps parallel shocks, not the 6 prescribed Basel scenarios. Worse of the two (+100bps parallel: -$1,822M before-tax total EVE impact) / Tier 1 capital as at July 31, 2024 ($95,724M, from Q4 2024 Pillar 3 KM1 table). This is a deviation from the strict 6-scenario definition since RBC does not publish that table.
notes.irrbbNiiSensitivityPct: Worse of the two disclosed shocks (-100bps parallel: -$425M before-tax 12-month NII impact) / same Tier 1 capital base ($95,724M).
notes.newMetricsSource: Q3 2024 Report to Shareholders (MD&A: Liquidity and Funding Risk, Market Risk sections) — https://www.rbc.com/investor-relations/_assets-custom/pdf/2024q3_report.pdf

irrbbDisclosureNote: RBC assesses IRRBB using two primary metrics — Net Interest Income (NII) risk and Economic Value of Equity (EVE) risk — under a range of market shocks internally, but its published disclosure ('Market risk measures - IRRBB sensitivities', in every quarterly Report to Shareholders MD&A and the Annual Report) shows only two scenarios: an immediate and sustained +100bps and -100bps parallel rate shock. It does not publish the full Basel/OSFI six-scenario table (parallel up/down, steepener, flattener, short-rate up/down). For each scenario RBC discloses before-tax dollar impacts on EVE and on 12-month NII, split by Canadian-dollar and U.S.-dollar-and-other currency impact plus a total; it does not itself express these as a percentage of Tier 1 capital — that conversion was computed by us using Tier 1 capital dollar figures separately disclosed in RBC's Pillar 3 KM1 tables. Disclosure frequency is quarterly, not merely annual — better coverage than most peers.
irrbbDisclosureSourceName: 2025 Annual Report, MD&A, 'Market risk measures - IRRBB Sensitivities' (Table 49); same format in each quarterly Report to Shareholders
